title: The first batch
subtitle: What is happening on this site, and what comes next. 8 panels.
rule: Every line a character says is the storyboard's, not a quote. What is said to happen is what the brief and the memo of 20 October 2026 say; what exists is in docs/reality.md.

scenes.title: The first batch
scenes.subtitle: What is happening here, and what comes next.

scenes.caption: First us, then the agents we already run
scenes.note: The memo of 20 October: the main users are the lead, the co-founder and the agents the lead already runs.

scenes.caption: Every agent needs a behaviour policy of its own

cast.says: Mine says what I may touch.

scenes.note: The wired-in agent gets the job of producing the end behaviour policy for the others.

scenes.caption: Every day, three questions

cast.says: What did you do? What got in the way? What's next?

scenes.note: Hand-holding on purpose. It will not scale, and it is not meant to yet.

scenes.caption: Seven steps, shared by everyone in the batch
scenes.note: The objectives are each customer's own; the steps are the shared shape, so the batch reads in one table.

scenes.caption: Every page has a price, and we learn the fair one

cast.says: Would I pay for that page?

scenes.note: The credit tells us how much each customer uses before they would top up; the follow-up tells us why.

scenes.caption: Everyone who asks is kept for the next batch
scenes.note: Capacity is limited, so the programme is one people propose to join.

scenes.punchline: The usage moment: when it becomes worth something to you.
scenes.note: The simplest useful behaviour policy, the entry with least friction, and the price that feels fair.
